_doc: The inputs of tools/build_seaslugs.py (the sea-slug species list, its popularity signals and the circles proposal; docs/reviews/2026-11-15-seaslug-list.md). Hand-kept: the tool reads this file and never writes it. roots: the iNaturalist taxa of the subject (Pierre, 2026-11-15, Q369 a: one subject, 'sea slugs'; the study's groups). area: the subject's own area for commonness (Q369 b: sea slugs ranked over the whole Philippines; the instance centre, tools/instance.json, still gives 'seen near Dauin'). wiki: the English Wikipedia pageviews window (the study's). nicknames: diver nicknames, each counted for a species only when its English Wikipedia title redirects to that species' article (checked by the tool); `ask` = not counted, a question for Pierre; `also` = other species Pierre decided share it, counted with the first (`why`: his words and the record). pages: the public pages read for mentions (scope ph = about Philippine sites, general = not tied to a place, out = about a place outside the Philippines: listed, not counted). stars: the stars set's size and Pierre's edits (add / remove: species names). circles: the proposal's sizes.

nicknames.title: Pikachu nudibranch
nicknames.why: Pierre, 2026-11-19 (Q417; docs/decisions/2026-11-19-pikachu-nickname.md): divers use Pikachu for more than one species, so it counts for T. pacifica (the redirect's) and T. pikachu (named after it, 2026); T. picta is only mentioned in the names.

nicknames.title: Spanish dancer
nicknames.ask: Pages and Wikipedia say 'Spanish dancer' for either Hexabranchus species; H. lacer is the one mostly recorded in the Philippines (study 2.3).

nicknames.title: Blue dragon
nicknames.ask: 'Blue dragon' often means Glaucus (not a Philippine reef slug) on general pages; Wikipedia's 'Blue Dragon' is not a sea slug.

nicknames.title: Shaun the sheep sea slug
nicknames.ask: No Wikipedia redirect; dive pages use it for Costasiella in general (study 4.2).

stars.why: Pierre, 2026-11-15, Q377 ('oui à tout' to #950's questions): 20 stars by the score, without the three that rested on one long list (the next scores replace them), plus H. lacer, the Spanish dancer recorded in the Philippines.

circles.why: Pierre, 2026-11-15, Q377: circle 1 of 45 (the stars plus the most common), later circles by commonness alone, 60, then 100, then the rest.

lookalikes.why: The two Spanish dancers: pages and Wikipedia say 'Spanish dancer' for either; WoRMS accepts both, citing Tibiriçá et al. 2023 (study 2.3, 6.3).

seaslug.world, Thecacera pikachu species page, https://en.seaslug.world/species/thecacera_pikachu (after Pola E., Paz-Sedano S., Martín J., Warren L., Noble L. & Martín-Hervás M.R. 2026. Zootaxa 5793(1): 193-217, https://doi.org/10.11646/zootaxa.5793.1.9): "T. pikachu has black spots all over the body, and its tips are plain black; T. pacifica has no spots on the body, and its tips are blue-white with a black band below" (read: the species page (2026-11-17); the paper's abstract only, not its full text).
lookalikes.decided: Q390 D (Pierre, 2026-11-17; paraphrase): the specialist-sourced species pairs declared; this set recorded in #1164

lookalikes.why: seaslug.world, Chromodoris alcalai species page, https://en.seaslug.world/species/chromodoris_alcalai (after Gosliner T.M. 2021. Sleuthing cryptic chromodorids (Mollusca, Nudibranchia): adding to Philippine marine biodiversity. Philippine Journal of Systematic Biology 14(2), https://doi.org/10.26757/pjsb2020b14014): "Morphologically very similar to Chromodoris dianae, with which it had been confused prior to formal description; separated by molecular evidence, external morphology, colour pattern, and internal anatomy" (read: the species page (2026-11-17); the paper not read (its DOI answered 503 on 2026-11-15)).
lookalikes.decided: Q390 D (Pierre, 2026-11-17; paraphrase): the specialist-sourced species pairs declared; this set recorded in #1164

photos.juvenileRule: +5 only where a source documents a different-looking juvenile

juvenile.Hexabranchus lacer: Documented: Tibiriçá et al. 2023, Fig. 3 'Ontogeny, color, and variation in Hexabranchus lacer' (its Plazi treatment), and the Sea Slug Forum's 'Juvenile Hexabranchus from Philippines' (Rudman, 1999, an animal from Dauin); docs/reviews/2026-11-15-seaslug-sources.md 1.5. The +5 holds Life Stage: Juvenile observations (tools/fetch_seaslugs.py).

photos.why: Pierre, 2026-11-15, Q377 (docs/reviews/2026-11-15-seaslug-list.md 5.3); revisit after the first judging pass.

exclude.eggs: Egg ribbons and egg masses are never candidates (Pierre, 2026-11-15). (1) Drop an observation annotated with one of `annotations` ([iNaturalist term, value]: Life Stage: Egg; Evidence of Presence: Egg), read from the observation's own annotations: no request parameter removes them exactly. (2) Judging: drop a photo whose subject is an egg mass (ribbon, coil, rosette, capsules) with no whole animal recognisable, and a photo that cannot be told apart from one; the recognisable animal with its eggs beside it is judged as an animal photo; the observation's other photos stay (rule P4). Juveniles stay in. docs/reviews/2026-11-15-seaslug-sources.md 1.4.
